reason: Nectar scales are scale-like nectaries in the flower, so flower nectary fits.
French 'squamule nectarifère' means a nectar-bearing scale, which is a flower nectary.
Plural of R2252; same meaning.
Nectar-bearing scale, i.e. a nectary. Same meaning as R2252.
An anther appendage can be an extension of the connective, but it can also be a spur or awn on the thecae (e.g. Ericaceae). Mapping all of them to the connective is wrong. The anther is safer.
Plural of R2255; same problem.
An apical appendage is often a connective prolongation, but not always. The rule loses the generic meaning, and the anther is safer.
French equivalent of R2255; same problem.
'Perianth part' is generic. In a flower with calyx and corolla it means a sepal or petal, so tepal is too specific.
Plural of R2259; same problem.
'Perianth segment' usually means a tepal. A lobe of a fused perianth is a rare exception.
Plural of R2261.
French 'pièce du périanthe' is generic and covers sepals, petals and tepals.
Plural of R2263; same problem.
'Perianth member' is generic and can be a sepal or petal as well as a tepal.
French 'foliole' means leaflet.
Plural of 'foliole'.
Latin 'foliolum' means leaflet.
'Bloom' alone often means flowers or flowering, not wax. It also means a glaucous coating. It cannot be mapped to epicuticular wax without context.
A waxy bloom is the epicuticular wax coating.

Fascicles also occur in leaves (pine needles), stamens (Hypericum), hairs, roots and vascular bundles. Flower fascicle fits only fascicles of flowers or inflorescences, so it needs a constraint on the container.
Singular of R2271; same problem. 'Fascicle' alone does not mean a flower cluster.
French 'fascicule' is equally generic: it is used for leaf, stamen and flower bundles.
Plural of R2273; same problem.
Endostome segments are the inner peristome. Peristome tooth would merge them with exostome teeth and lose the inner/outer distinction.
Plural of R2275; same problem.
Same as R2275; the endostome identity is lost.
Same as R2275; 'inner' is lost.
In ferns and seed plants the sporophyte is the whole plant. In bryophytes it is only the dependent capsule and seta, so it is not a whole plant.
Plural of R2279; same problem.
A spatheole is a small spathe, i.e. an inflorescence bract.
Plural of R2281.
French 'spathéole' is a small spathe, an inflorescence bract.
Plural of R2283.
A collective vein is the vein running close to the lamina margin, which is the intramarginal vein.
Plural of R2285.
'Collecting vein' is a variant of collective vein, i.e. the intramarginal vein.
Plural of R2287.
French 'nervure collectrice' is the collective (intramarginal) vein.
A rachilla is the ultimate inflorescence axis, such as a palm branchlet or a spikelet axis. It is a higher-order inflorescence axis.
Singular of R2290.
Spelling variant of rachilla.
French plural of rachille.
The PO lexicon lists gametophyte as a synonym of whole plant. It is acceptable for bryophyte or fern gametophytes.
Plural of R2294.
A cross-vein is a small connecting vein between main veins. Leaf lamina vein loses the 'connecting' meaning. The word is also used for insect wings.
Plural of R2296; same problem.
Spelling variant of R2296; same problem.
On a plant a secondary axis is a branch. In an inflorescence it is a second-order axis, which is a higher order inflorescence axis (PO_0009081), not a branch.
Plural of R2299; same problem.
